target.title: Add Grok weekly usage projections
target.body:
## Summary

- Enable the existing reset-window pace projection for Grok weekly quota windows.
- Classify reset-based Grok windows using the menu model deterministic timestamp.
- Cover CLI and web weekly windows, plus monthly and unclassified negative cases.

## Why

Grok was excluded from the generic reset-window pace support used by other providers. Web-derived Grok windows also relied on the wall clock during label classification instead of the model input timestamp, which prevented deterministic weekly classification in the menu model.

The shared `UsagePace.weekly` helper remains responsible for validating reset timing and window duration.

## User impact

Weekly Grok usage rows with a valid weekly reset now show the existing deficit/reserve text, projected run-out estimate, and pace marker. Monthly and unclassified windows remain unchanged.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter GrokMenuCardModelTests` — 4 tests passed
- `swift test --skip-build --filter Grok` — 48 tests passed
- `make check` — SwiftFormat and SwiftLint passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- Full sharded suite — discovered 643 selections; stopped after an unrelated `CLIOpenAIDashboardCacheTests` group reported 3 cache-restoration failures
- `swift test --skip-build --filter CLIOpenAIDashboardCacheTests` — all 10 tests passed in isolation

Fixes #2165

target.title: fix: confirm identity-less Claude reset samples
target.body:
## Summary

- require a second low-usage sample before celebrating a Claude reset when the observation has no account identity and therefore uses the shared `claude:claude` detector key
- preserve compatibility with previously persisted detector state
- add coverage for a transient simultaneous session/weekly low sample followed by recovery, plus a real reset confirmed by the next sample

## Root cause

Identity-less Claude CLI probe samples share one persisted detector key. A transient partial/near-zero CLI read can therefore look like a reset for both the session and weekly windows. The detector previously posted immediately on the first threshold crossing.

## Behavior

Only the low-confidence shared Claude path waits for one subsequent low sample (one refresh interval). Identified accounts retain the existing immediate behavior.

## Test

- `swift test --filter "UsageStorePlanUtilizationTests"` (72 tests passed)

Fixes #2222.

target.title: fix(vydra): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users generating Vydra images/audio/video would hang when the CDN returned response headers and then dripped the body slowly enough to keep resetting the per-chunk idle timer. `fetchWithTimeout` is designed to clear its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body read.

Same hang class as Discord probe / ClawHub: idle can be reset by drip; wall-clock must span the body. This includes both successful asset bodies and non-2xx error-detail bodies (ClawSweeper P2 on the first review).

## Why This Change Was Made

At the `downloadVydraAsset` call site only, keep one wall-clock deadline across headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` / `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`, matching Discord `probe.ts` / `readDiscordProbeGetMeJson`. Shared `fetchWithTimeout` and `assertOkOrThrowHttpError` are intentionally unchanged.

Does not change request-policy / SSRF work in open PRs such as #105884 / #109080 — those remain complementary. If #105884 lands first and keeps abort until `release()`, this call-site deadline is still the Discord-shaped body bound and remains correct.

This PR was AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Vydra media downloads now fail within the configured HTTP timeout when a remote body keeps trickling instead of completing — for both 2xx asset bodies and dripping non-2xx error bodies. Image/speech/video generation no longer sticks forever on a slow drip CDN response.

## Evidence

### Behavior addressed
- Before (2xx): headers arrive → `fetchWithTimeout` cleanup → body only has `chunkTimeoutMs` → drip every 20ms resets idle → hang until process/test timeout.
- Before (non-2xx): `assertOkOrThrowHttpError` reads error detail without a wall-clock bound → drip every 20ms resets idle → hang before the success-path reader runs.
- After: same drip on 200 or 500 fails with `Vydra image download timed out after <timeoutMs>ms` inside the wall-clock budget.

### Exact commands

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/vydra/shared.test.ts
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/vydra/
```

### Focused regression (3 passed) — head `391009428f4`

```
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-media.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Duration  7.78s (transform 5.40s, setup 651ms, import 5.93s, tests 1.02s, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.89s
```

Covers:
- dripping 200 asset body → wall-clock timeout
- dripping 500 error body → wall-clock timeout
- idle-only negative control stays unsettled past 400ms

### Sibling vydra suite (21 passed / 5 files)

```
 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
   Duration  20.76s (transform 15.29s, setup 560ms, import 18.73s, tests 1.30s, environment 0ms)
```

### Autoreview

```
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted --base origin/main --engine claude
→ autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
→ overall: patch is correct (0.97)
```

(Codex engine returned 401 Unauthorized in this environment; Claude engine used as fallback.)

### What was NOT tested
- Live `vydra.ai` CDN hang (exercised real `downloadVydraAsset` + Node fetch against loopback drip for both 200 and 500 instead).
- Did not change shared `src/utils/fetch-timeout.ts` or `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.
